_note: JSON has no comment syntax, so this key carries one. Three shapes here are deliberate and none of them is a typo. (1) `domains[0]` is what the `domain` entity writes: id, no dates. `domains[1]` is what the `knowledge` entity writes into the SAME list (its `category` defaults to "domains"): added_date/last_updated and NO id -- persona_store._assign_ids would backfill the id on the next backend save, which is exactly why the renderer must not depend on one. (2) `mental_tabs[2]` carries the legacy `topic` key with no `title`: never written by any current code path, still read as a fallback in four places in server.py. It renders with a blank title on purpose -- the manifest binds `title` and nothing else -- and the test beside it asserts that `topic` and every other key survive an edit regardless. persona_store._normalize backfills `title` from `topic` on load, so a blob that has been through the backend does not look like this; this entry is the renderer's own guard against key loss, independent of that repair. (3) `related` appears on two entries and is bound by nothing: it is the link graph, written only by _execute_link and rendered nowhere, so the only thing asked of it is that it survives. This key itself is inert -- no ui node addresses it.
